title: Legal Standards / Disclaimers & Other Fine Print
slide_intent: Give qualifying information deliberate typographic treatment so readers can distinguish it from promotional copy and still read it.
strategic_value: Specific print and television treatments can help Burger King maintain readable conditions alongside persuasive communications.
demonstration: A left section heading accompanies a narrow text column specifying print disclaimer treatment, US type sizes and television contrast/scan-line guidance.
practical_value: Separate the historical US print and television specifications from the instruction to obtain guidance for other countries.

content_islands.name: Section heading
content_islands.spec: Place the three-line fine-print heading at left.

content_islands.name: Print treatment
content_islands.spec: Begin the adjacent text column with bolding guidance and the US 8-point disclaimer and 5-point legal-line preferences.

content_islands.name: Television treatment
content_islands.spec: Continue below with black-background white-type guidance, other-background shadow treatment and the outside-US referral.

reference_purposes.Intent: The text connects bolding to distinction from sales copy and readability, and drop shadows to television legibility.
reference_purposes.Application: The page describes print and television treatments separately.
reference_purposes.Constraint: Historical US preferences are 8-point printed disclaimers and 5-point trademark/copyright lines; black-background TV disclaimers use at least 22 scan lines in 100% white. Other TV backgrounds use a drop shadow; outside-US cases go to Legal.

ingredient.name: Disclaimer typography
ingredient.role: Keep qualifying information distinguishable and readable.
ingredient.application: Follow the source’s medium-specific treatments: bold print disclaimers; US preferred sizes of 8 pt for disclaimers and 5 pt for legal lines; US black-background TV uses at least 22 scan lines in 100% white, with drop shadows on other backgrounds.
ingredient.scope: Historical 2020 guide statements, not current legal advice. Requirements vary by country; the page refers outside-US treatment to Burger King Legal.
